decisive_items: rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on her extremities
The patient had no remarkable medical or family history
The palms, soles, and oral mucosa were not involved
response.rationale: Grover's disease best matches the acute pruritic papular eruption in an older adult with no family history, dyskeratosis/parakeratosis, and eosinophilic dermal infiltrate; Darier's disease is less likely because it is typically chronic, autosomal dominant, with seborrheic distribution and frequent nail/mucosal involvement, all absent here.

rejected.why: Darier's disease is usually a chronic autosomal dominant genodermatosis with adolescent onset and seborrheic distribution; the acute pruritic extremity eruption in a 50-year-old with no family history and spared palms/soles/mucosa is atypical, and cornoid lamellae are not characteristic of Darier's.
